CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc who presents for annual exam. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since steroid injection several months ago with no back pain or limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel release from a couple of years ago is also doing well with full range of motion and no recurrent issues; she has returned to work. Regarding her coronary artery disease, she reports chest pain over the last month that occurs with walking and resolves with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest occurring approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses chest pain and nasal congestion from allergies due to pollen. She denies lower extremity edema, muscle aches, or fever and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is back at work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation fine. Heart: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no carotid bruits appreciated. Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Skin: Healed surgical scars on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year showed slightly low pumping function at 45% and mild mitral regurgitation. EKG reviewed showing stable results reflecting prior coronary artery disease with no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Carpal tunnel release: No further intervention needed at this time; patient doing well with return to work. If recurrent symptoms develop, patient to notify provider. Herniated disc: No further steroid injection or physical therapy needed at this time. If recurrent symptoms develop, patient to notify provider. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Continue aspirin and Toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Order lipid panel. Start Crestor 20 mg once daily. Nurse will assist with scheduling tests.
